title: Pilot killed in small plane crash near regional airport in Florida
byline: The pilot of a small plane was killed after the single-engine aircraft crashed near Space Coast Regional Airport in Titusville, Florida, officials said on Monday.

title: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 jobs over next two years
byline: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is to cut 4,000 jobs as the carmaker struggles with Chinese competition, US tariffs, and the transition to electric vehicles.

title: Rs. 130 Mn assets frozen in Money Laundering probe
byline: Sri Lanka Police have frozen properties worth more than Rs. 130 million allegedly acquired through proceeds from illegal drug trafficking, the Illegal Assets Investigation Division said.

title: Traffic restrictions announced for Rajnath Singh’s Sri Lanka visit
byline: Special traffic arrangements will be in place in Colombo and surrounding areas from September 8 to 10 in connection with the official visit of Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to Sri Lanka.

title: Southern Expressway service area land leased for 99 years
byline: The property used for a service area on the Southern Expressway was leased for 99 years at an annual rent of just Rs. 10,000 during the previous Rajapaksa administration, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake revealed.

title: Sri Lanka reaffirms commitment to UN engagement ahead of UNGA
byline: Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath met with United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka Marc-André Franche at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism this morning.

title: Appeals open for 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship Exam answer sheets
byline: The Department of Examinations has called for online appeals regarding the 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship Examination, conducted to select students for schools and award scholarships.

title: Namal to attend Parliament tomorrow following Secretary General’s response
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser, Attorney-at-Law Namal Rajapaksa, is scheduled to attend Parliament tomorrow (8), following arrangements made in response to his request for the necessary facilities to participate in parliamentary sittings.

title: CSE starts week steady as indices edge higher amid balanced trading
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange opened the week on a relatively flat note on Monday, 7 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing marginally higher following a volatile trading session.

title: Parliament Committee questions police officials over cyclone Ditwah response
byline: The Parliamentary Select Committee appointed to conduct a comprehensive study into the lack of preparedness to face Cyclone Ditwah has questioned senior Sri Lanka Police officers who were involved in responding to the disaster.

title: China saw it. India saw it. The world is moving in. Sri Lanka cannot afford to arrive late
byline: Africa is rapidly shedding its outdated image of instability to emerge as the world’s next economic powerhouse. Driven by a young, expanding workforce, vast natural wealth, and a firm resolve to shift from raw material exporter to industrial manufacturer, the continent presents unprecedented opportunities. Global giants like China and India recognized this trajectory early and built deep roots.

title: Kevin Pietersen returns to England as White-Ball Mentor
byline: Pietersen, 46, joins as a specialist mentor and will start in the role for the upcoming T20 and one-day matches against Sri Lanka.

title: Over 8,500 fake-labelled water bottles ordered to be destroyed
byline: The Avissawella Magistrate’s Court has ordered the destruction of more than 8,500 bottles of drinking water seized from a company in Seethawaka for allegedly using a counterfeit SLS standard logo and misleading consumers with an unauthorised brand name.

title: Ampitiye Sumanarathana Thera remanded until tomorrow
byline: Venerable Ampitiye Sumanarathana Thera, who was arrested by Batticaloa Police today, has been remanded until tomorrow (7) after being produced before the Batticaloa Magistrate’s Court.

title: Reservoir storage remains at 34.3% as yesterday
byline: Water storage in Sri Lanka’s major reservoirs stood at 34.3% of effective capacity as of yesterday (September 6), data released by the Irrigation Department’s Water Management Branch said.

title: Clean Air Day highlights need for healthier choices
byline: The International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies is being observed today (September 7), highlighting the importance of clean air for healthy lives, resilient communities and a sustainable future.

title: Special regulations introduced to protect Nildiya Pokuna
byline: The Ministry of Environment has introduced special regulations to ensure the sustainable management and long-term conservation of Nildiya Pokuna, located within the Ravana Ella Sanctuary.

title: PM calls for ‘cultured’ society amid social media abuse
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has highlighted the need to build a more cultured and sensitive society, saying certain comments made on social media, particularly those targeting children, women and vulnerable people, highlight the need for greater humanity in public discourse.

title: Nepal observes national day of mourning for victims of flash flood disaster
byline: Nepalis observed a national day of mourning for the victims of the flash flood on Monday, lighting candles to mark the last day of the traditional 13-day Hindu mourning period.

title: Pinnawala Zoo unveils three leopard cubs on World Cat Day
byline: Pinnawala Zoo marked World Cat Day with a special educational programme featuring the public debut of three leopard cubs born at the zoo.

title: Far-right AfD wins historic victory in German state election
byline: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting ​a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two.

title: ‘Vasana’ elephant to be used only for major peraheras
byline: The Ruhunu Maha Kataragama Devalaya has decided to restrict the participation of its ‘Vasana’ elephant to major peraheras in a move aimed at protecting the animal’s health and well-being.

title: Further evidence in bribery case against Kumara Jayakody fixed for October 5
byline: Colombo High Court Judge Rasantha Godawela ordered that the further trial of evidence in the case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) against former Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody over an alleged corruption offence be taken up on October 5.

title: Metro bus fleet to reach 172 as service expands nationwide
byline: The government plans to expand the Metro Bus Service to 172 buses by the end of this year or early next year, with the programme also expected to extend beyond the Western Province to Galle, Kandy and Jaffna.

title: Yoshitha Rajapaksa withdraws appeal before Supreme Court in money laundering case
byline: The Supreme Court today granted permission to former President Mahinda Rajapaksa’s son Yoshitha Rajapaksa to withdraw an appeal challenging the Court of Appeal decision to dismiss a revision application relating to a money-laundering case.

title: Health reforms must move beyond projects and paperwork: Expert
byline: Sri Lanka needs to move away from a healthcare system dominated by bureaucracy, workshops and policy documents and focus more strongly on practical results for the public, health expert Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa has said.

title: Special security for Namal Rajapaksa at remand prison
byline: Special security arrangements have been implemented in and around the ward where Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa is being held at the Colombo Remand Prison, according to the Department of Prisons.

title: UN finds little progress on justice in Sri Lanka
byline: Seventeen years after the end of Sri Lanka’s civil war, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has raised concerns over the lack of accountability for alleged grave human rights violations and international crimes committed during the conflict.

title: North Korea deploys warship ‘capable of annihilating retaliatory strikes’
byline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended the commissioning of a warship he said could deliver “annihilating retaliatory strikes on an enemy”, citing “constant threats”, according to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

title: Second Metro Bus Depot begins operations
byline: Sri Lanka’s second metro bus depot, constructed in Kadawatha, commenced operations today as part of efforts to modernise and expand the country’s public transport system.

title: Customs seizes Rs. 51.37 million worth of Kush and Hashish at BIA
byline: Sri Lanka Customs Narcotics Control Unit officers have seized 5.137 kilograms of Kush cannabis and hashish worth an estimated Rs. 51.37 million from two Thai nationals at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA).

title: Chamal Rajapaksa appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Former MP Chamal Rajapaksa arrived at the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning (08) to provide a statement in connection with an ongoing investigation into alleged financial irregularities surrounding the procurement of Airbus aircraft for SriLankan Airlines.

title: Turtle conservation programme held at Adam’s Bridge Marine National Park
byline: A special awareness programme was held on September 3 to evaluate the progress of the “Sea Turtle Nest Observation Programme – 2026”, conducted as part of ongoing sea turtle conservation efforts at the Adam’s Bridge Marine National Park in Talaimannar.

title: ‘I’m not a war criminal’: Shavendra Silva hits back at Western sanctions
byline: Former Sri Lanka Army Commander and Chief of Defence Staff General Shavendra Silva has defended the military’s conduct during the final stages of the country’s civil war, rejecting allegations of war crimes and criticising the sanctions imposed on him by Western governments.

title: Over 200 kg of fish caught using dynamite ordered destroyed
byline: More than 200 kilograms of fish seized following an illegal fishing operation involving dynamite have been ordered destroyed by court order after authorities determined that the stock was unfit for human consumption.

title: Some clauses of Chartered Institute of Media Professionals Bill inconsistent with Constitution
byline: The Supreme Court has held that some sections of the  Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka is inconsistent with the Constitution and has to be approved by a special majority in Parliament, Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne said today.

title: INS Udaygiri makes port call in Colombo
byline: Indian Naval Ship (INS) Udaygiri arrived at the Port of Colombo today, September 8, 2026, on an official visit to Sri Lanka. The vessel was received by the Sri Lanka Navy in accordance with longstanding naval traditions.

title: Paid leave essential to workers’ health and well-being
byline: Sri Lanka’s workers are already entitled to a range of paid leave and holidays, but as workplaces become increasingly connected, a greater concern may be whether employees are actually able to switch off when they take time away from work.

title: SDIG Ajith Rohana retires after 38 years of service
byline: Senior Deputy Inspector General of Police (SDIG) Attorney-at-Law Dr. Ajith Rohana retired today after completing an illustrious 38-year career in Sri Lanka Police. A ceremonial police guard of honour was held at the Welagedara Stadium in Kurunegala to mark his retirement and honour his longstanding service to the country.

title: Family doctor system must not threaten free healthcare
byline: The proposed introduction of a family doctor system in Sri Lanka should be implemented in a manner that strengthens, rather than undermines, the country’s free healthcare system, Medical and Civil Rights Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance Chairman and Specialist Dr Chamal Sanjeewa said.

title: Solicitor General appointed Acting Attorney General
byline: Solicitor General Viraj Dayaratne, PC, has been appointed as the Acting Attorney General by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: New education reforms to focus on inclusive education: Deputy Minister
byline: The new education reforms will place greater emphasis on inclusive education to ensure that no child is left behind and that all students receive equal educational opportunities, Deputy Minister of Education and Higher Education Dr. Madura Seneviratne said.

title: Education key to promoting equality and mutual respect: PM
byline: Education is the most powerful tool to create public understanding of mutual respect and equality, Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Dr. Harini Amarasuriya said.

title: University lecturers to strike tomorrow, FUTA says
byline: University lecturers have decided to launch a one-day strike tomorrow (9), the Federation of University Teachers’ Associations (FUTA) said.

title: Government mulls action against all connected to Airbus deal
byline: Following the arrest of Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa in connection with the controversial Airbus deal, Transport Minister Bimal Rathnayake said the Government was not engaged in political revenge and was only acting within its legal mandate.

title: Seat belt rule to be strictly enforced on Expressways from September 19
byline: The mandatory seat belt regulation on expressways will be strictly enforced from September 19, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake said in Parliament today.

title: Work on three new expressways to begin this year: Minister
byline: Work on three expressways, namely Katunayake -Chilaw, Kurunegala -Dambulla and Kahatuduwa -Ingiriya, will begin this year, Minister of Transport Bimal Ratnayake told Parliament today.

title: El Niño may increase human-elephant conflict, Wildlife DG warns
byline: The ongoing El Niño conditions could increase the risk of wild elephants roaming into human settlements in search of food and water, Director General of Wildlife Ranjan Marasinghe has warned.

title: China readies humanoid robots for combat
byline: At the World Humanoid Robot Games in China last month, robots jumped, boxed and danced. Some fleet-footed bots ran faster than Usain Bolt over 100 meters. Spectators cheered the machines’ improving capabilities and their meme-worthy stumbles.

title: Namal arrives in Parliament on prison bus
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa arrived at Parliament in a prison bus today to participate in parliamentary sittings.

title: Preventing stroke: The role of physiotherapy in building a healthier Sri Lanka
byline: Every year on 8 September, the global physiotherapy community celebrates World Physiotherapy Day, recognizing the contribution of physiotherapists to health, wellbeing and quality of life. In 2026, the theme focuses on the role of physiotherapy and physical activity in the prevention, management and rehabilitation of cardiovascular disease and stroke.

title: Profitable Lanka Sathosa outlets face closure as property owners reclaim buildings
byline: Several profitable Lanka Sathosa outlets have been forced to close, while others are facing possible closure after property owners sought the return of buildings leased to the state-run retailer, Deputy Minister of Trade, Commerce and Food Security R. M. Jayawardhana told Parliament.

title: Australia targets social media algorithms with new user-choice rules
byline: Australia on Tuesday proposed giving social media users the option to select the content they see on their feeds, marking the next step in the government’s ​push to improve online safety, following its world-first social media ban for children.

title: 2018 soldier murder probe: CID arrests victim’s wife
byline: The wife of a retired soldier who was allegedly abducted and murdered in the Kirindiwela area has been arrested by the Homicide and Organised Crime Investigation Division of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

title: Commonwealth Lawyers Association raises questions over Supreme Court proceedings
byline: In a nine-page report, President of the Commonwealth Lawyers Association (CLA) Steven Thiru has raised several concerns over procedural fairness, transparency and the composition of the Supreme Court bench that heard petitions challenging the constitutionality of the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution.

title: Where have our fish gone?
byline: Sri Lanka is witnessing a significant decline in its stocks of small pelagic fish, including sardines, sardinellas and anchovies, with the standing stock of pelagic species now estimated at only around 20,000 tonnes in the surveyed waters, according to Norwegian fisheries scientist Jens-Otto Krakstad.

title: Kiriwehera Chief Incumbent’s vehicle involved in road accident
byline: The vehicle carrying Venerable Kobawaka Dhamminda Thero, Chief Incumbent of the Kataragama Kiriwehera Rajamaha Viharaya, was involved in a road accident in the Mattala area last night (07).

title: Indonesia airports reopen after volcano eruption leaves 340,000 stranded
byline: Indonesia reopened five airports past midnight on Tuesday, after a volcanic eruption over the weekend forced them to suspend operations for two days.

title: Nuwara Eliya records lowest minimum temperature at 13.5°C
byline: Nuwara Eliya recorded the lowest minimum temperature in Sri Lanka at 13.5°C, according to temperature observations issued by the Meteorology Department today.

title: Eiffel Tower shut by staff protest after female workers moved for religious visit
byline: The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday after staff went on strike over female workers being removed for the visit of a Hindu religious group, workers and management said.

title: Why Thailand ended visa-free entry for Sri Lankans: Herath explains
byline: Illegal activities allegedly committed by Sri Lankan nationals while using Thailand’s visa-free facility contributed to the decision to end visa-free entry for Sri Lankan passport holders, Cabinet Spokesman and Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: Don’t suppress right of people to seek hospital treatment when they fall sick: Namal
byline: Referring to a remark made by President Anura Kumara Dissannayake that people should reduce the number of their hospital visits, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa said the government should not suppress the people’s right to seek hospital treatment when they fall sick.

title: Iran-backed Houthis attack four Saudi cities in expansion of Middle East war, 73 hurt
byline: Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in the south of U.S. ally Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people ​and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war.

title: Digital Transformation Units to be established in government institutions
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to establish dedicated Digital Transformation Units in government institutions to coordinate and manage digital transformation initiatives.

title: Colombo Marathon 2026 to be held on September 13
byline: The “Colombo Marathon – 2026” international marathon competition will be held at Galle Face Green, Colombo, on September 13, in conjunction with the 50th National Games.

title: Sri Lanka, Thailand to sign agreements on labour cooperation
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Labour Cooperation and a supplementary agreement governing the employment of Sri Lankan workers in Thailand for a period of five years.

title: Cabinet approves new Bill to combat organised crime
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the publication of a new draft Bill aimed at preventing and combating organised crime in Sri Lanka.

title: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh arrived in Sri Lanka today (08) for a three-day official visit aimed at further strengthening defence cooperation between India and Sri Lanka.

title: Railway Controllers Union supports Sept. 17 strike
byline: The Railway Controllers Union has announced its support for the token strike scheduled to be launched by the Railway Joint Trade Union Alliance from midnight on September 17.

title: Galle school principal arrested over Rs. 250,000 bribe
byline: The Principal of Buonavista College in Galle was arrested by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) while allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs. 250,000.

title: Private-sector employees to get online railway season tickets from October 1
byline: Sri Lanka Railways will introduce an online facility for private-sector employees to obtain monthly railway season tickets from October 1, through the official seat reservation website.

title: 13-year-old schoolboy drowns in Maoya
byline: A 13-year-old schoolboy drowned in the Maha Oya near Yakabendiella, while his father, who attempted to save him, also got into difficulty.

title: U.S alerts Sri Lanka over Iranian vessels off its waters
byline: The U.S. Embassy in Colombo has informed Sri Lanka’s Foreign Ministry about the presence of several Iranian vessels in international waters and inquired whether authorities were aware of them and monitoring their movements, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: UK announces sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements
byline: United Kingdom Foreign Minister Ed Miliband has announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

title: CSE retreats as broad-based selling pulls ASPI below 21,550
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange reversed its recent positive momentum on Tuesday, 8 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing lower amid broad-based selling pressure.

title: Foreign Minister to represent Sri Lanka at UN General Assembly
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake will not attend this year’s United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), with Sri Lanka to be represented at ministerial level, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said today (08).

title: Government introduces multi-purpose loan scheme for Sri Lankan migrant workers
byline: The Government has introduced a multi-purpose loan scheme to help Sri Lankan migrant workers make productive use of their overseas earnings for housing, education, business and other financial needs.

title: Apple’s new iPhone lineup to be unveiled tomorrow night: What Sri Lankans need to know, and will a foldable iPhone finally debut?
byline: Apple unveils its new iPhone lineup on September 9, with rumours pointing to its first-ever foldable model. Here’s when to watch from Sri Lanka and what could be announced.

title: Journalists missing in Indonesia after volcano mission
byline: Indonesian teams were searching on Tuesday for seven people including five journalists who had gone missing while travelling to cover the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau, the national rescue agency said.

title: UK announces sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements
byline: United Kingdom Foreign Minister Ed Miliband has announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
